subject: Keep-or-Purge checklist: what Redwood stores by default (requests vs outputs)
messages:
From: Nora Li <nora@clearwave.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Retention question — what you keep by default (prompts vs outputs)

Hi Sean,

We're preparing our Data Processing Agreement and I want to be explicit about Redwood's default behaviour. Can you confirm the following in plain language for our legal/infosec review?

- By default, does Redwood store the raw user prompt (user-submitted text) separately from the model output?
- Are streamed tokens (fragmented outputs while streaming) treated differently from the 'final' generated answer?
- What is the default retention window for: (a) requests/prompts, (b) model responses/outputs, (c) low-level debug traces (token-level logs), (d) KV cache/stream-state, and (e) attachment metadata (filenames)
- How does a customer opt-out of storage for requests/outputs (is there an API flag or account-level setting)?

We need short answers and a one-line description of the deletion/evidence path we can reference in the contract. Also, if there are standard enterprise exceptions (shorter windows), please outline those.

Thanks — Nora
Nora Li
Head of Security Programs, ClearWave

---
Note: attaching our template NDA redline request separately (not included here).

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Nora Li <nora@clearwave.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention question — what you keep by default (prompts vs outputs)

Hi Nora — quick summary below, then I include next steps and an internal cc for procedure/evidence. Short answers first:

- Do we store prompt vs output?
  Short: Yes — both the submitted request (prompt) and the final model output are retained by default as separate artifacts. We keep them to support billing, debugging, and quality monitoring.

- Streamed tokens vs final answer?
  Short: Stream fragments are stored temporarily (stream buffer) and treated as transient; only the final serialized output is treated as the canonical artifact for long-term retention unless you opt-in to keep stream fragments for diagnostics.

- Default retention windows (default tenant settings):
  (a) Requests / prompts: 90 days
  (b) Model outputs (final answers): 90 days
  (c) Debug traces / token-level logs: 90 days (kept at higher fidelity for troubleshooting; can be disabled)
  (d) KV cache / session state: session-scoped — cleared within 7 days by default and not indexed for search
  (e) Attachment metadata (filenames, mime-type): retained 90 days; actual attachment content follows customer upload rules (we keep a reference stub unless you upload to your own S3)

- Opt-out mechanisms:
  - API flag: store=false on request (for built-in endpoints) causes the request/output to be excluded from default store pipelines.
  - Account-level: Enterprise contracts can default to a shorter retention or turn off storage; we also support per-route policies in the Console.

Deletion/evidence path (one-line): by default artifacts are garbage-collected after the retention window and erasure is recorded in our deletion ledger; enterprise erasure evidence (proof-of-deletion package) can be provided on request via an internal runbook.

If you want a narrower default for ClearWave (e.g., 30-day window or token-trace off), we can propose that as a contract term and add it to the SOW. I’ve looped in Marissa from Sales for the commercial side.

Next steps:
- If you need the 30-day example contract language, say so and I’ll have Marissa prepare a short SOW clause.
- I’ll ask Ops to attach the runbook for deletion evidence to this thread.

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention-checklist-stub.pdf (see referenced runbook for full evidence pack)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: FWD: Retention question — ClearWave wants plain-language checklist / 30-day ask possible

Kimberly, Marissa — forwarding ClearWave's ask. They want plain-language answers for legal and an optional 30-day retention proposal. Can Ops/Legal confirm the following so I can give clear contract language?

Requests:
- Confirm the default windows above (we currently list 90d for requests/outputs and 7d for session state). Is that accurate for hosted tenants today?
- What fields are included in the deletion evidence package (hashes, timestamps, runbook steps)?
- Is 'store=false' implemented on all public endpoints or only on specific SDKs? Any known gaps?

If we can offer a 30-day enterprise default (requests+outputs+token-traces off) how quickly can we ship that as a contractual setting? Also, the customer asked for an example one-line deletion summary we can add to their DPA.

Please reply with a short checklist I can paste into an email.

Onward — Sean

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Retention question — ClearWave wants plain-language checklist / 30-day ask possible

Sean — quick operational checklist you can paste to the customer:

- Default windows (hosted API): requests/prompts = 90 days; final outputs = 90 days; debug/token traces = 90 days; streaming buffers/session-scoped KV = 7 days.
- Deletion evidence package contents: deletion timestamp + object ids, cryptographic digest of stored objects (SHA256), deletion runbook id, operator id, and retention policy version.
- API opt-out: store=false is available on all public REST endpoints and official SDKs today; it prevents storage in our long-term pipelines but short-lived streaming buffers may still exist until the request completes (buffer TTL=24h).
- Enterprise exceptions: we can contractually set retention to 30 days or shorter, and can disable token-level traces. SLA: changes applied after contract signature and a one-time configuration window (3–10 business days).

One-line deletion summary for DPA (suggested): "Redwood retains user-submitted requests and model-generated outputs by default for 90 days and permanently expunges those artifacts at the end of the retention period; upon request and under contract Redwood will apply a shorter retention period and provide a proof-of-deletion package."

Links for evidence / runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/retention-deletion-v2 (internal), HubSpot deal: https://crm.redwood.com/HubSpot/deal/CLR-1992

Kimberly
Director, Product Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
